strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Existing headless.run.drive can derive bounded product evidence from a request-supplied project completion policy artifact and completion ledger facts before product stop/continue decisions.
Product completion gates move from Brownie-specific runtime artifact paths to a generic policy boundary that the Rust runtime verifies before decisions.
Rust validates the derivation authorization, policy/evidence artifact hashes, symlink/file-kind checks, policy membership, completion claim, and completion-boundary binding.
Headless replay uses bounded fingerprints and category counts instead of raw Product Charter, manifest, spec, or ledger text.
Drive results can surface bounded next action to record a product decision using runtime-derived evidence.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting agent_loop, runtime_permission_enforcement, context_management, and progress_visualization.
answers.new_capability: Existing headless.run.drive can explicitly derive a bounded product evidence matrix from a generic project completion policy artifact, persist it once, replay it, and deny product_complete decisions when the policy claim is false.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M52.1 moved evidence derivation into Rust but embedded Brownie-specific artifact paths in the runtime, so the runtime still owned project strategy instead of enforcing a generic policy boundary.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A headless caller could not reuse product completion evidence authority for another repository/project without changing runtime code, and a false completion claim could still become a stop attempt.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M51.3.1 same-boundary uniqueness and M52.1 fixed-artifact matrix derivation because this changes ownership of the product completion policy itself and gates product_complete on the derived claim.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. This extends existing headless.run.drive rather than adding a JSON-RPC method.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The matrix is bounded runtime evidence used by the decision path, not a report/history/readiness/verdict/inspection/dashboard wrapper.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust validates explicit derivation authorization, request policy hash, policy-declared evidence artifact membership, expected SHA-256 hashes, regular UTF-8 non-symlink file kind, policy gate content, completion claim, and completion-boundary binding before ledger append or product decision consumption.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless callers can supply a bounded project policy and rely on Rust to derive whether the current evidence permits stop or requires continued development.
answers.milestone_progress: This turns M52 from a Brownie-specific evidence derivation into a reusable runtime-owned product completion policy boundary.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M52.2 updates manifests and runtime/protocol code for generic project completion policy derivation. Review must confirm guard enforcement is not weakened and this is not a report-only surface.

exit_criteria: headless.run.drive can derive a bounded product evidence matrix from a request-supplied project completion policy artifact with expected SHA-256 hashes
derived matrix evidence is bound to accepted-completion, terminal-completion, and completion-closure fingerprints
product_completion_decision consumes the derived matrix fingerprint and refuses product_complete when the policy-derived product_completion_claim is false
stale policy/evidence artifact hashes, unsafe artifacts, or artifacts that do not match policy membership fail closed before matrix or product-decision ledger mutation
replay is duplicate-free for matrix and product-decision evidence
no new JSON-RPC method and no report/readiness/history/verdict/inspection/dashboard wrapper is added

RPC and ledger metadata remain bounded and exclude raw prompts, provider responses, final responses, file content, raw Product Charter or manifest text, diagnostics, stdout/stderr, commands, environment, raw requests, raw ledger payloads, absolute paths, canonical paths, and secrets
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_derives_product_evidence_matrix_and_decides validates authorized policy-based matrix derivation, false-claim product_complete denial, continue_development decision consumption, replay, bounded metadata, and duplicate-free events.
Rust negative test headless_run_drive_rejects_stale_product_evidence_artifact_hash validates stale policy-declared evidence artifact hash denial before matrix or product-decision mutation.
VSIX runtimeClient protocol tests validate product_evidence_derivation, product_evidence_matrix, and derived_product_evidence_matrix_fingerprint transport shape without VSIX-owned policy.

accepted_capability: Existing headless.run.drive derives and persists bounded runtime-owned product evidence matrix metadata from a generic project completion policy for product completion decisions
safety_boundary: Request-supplied project completion policy must be a safe JSON artifact with expected SHA-256
Policy-declared evidence artifacts must exactly match requested artifact sources
Expected SHA-256 required for the policy and every evidence artifact
Existing regular UTF-8 non-symlink artifacts only
False product_completion_claim denies product_complete before product-decision ledger mutation
Completion boundary fingerprints must match before derivation and decision consumption
Ledger and RPC expose only bounded ids, counts, category names, artifact paths, hashes, next action, and SHA-256 fingerprints
VSIX validates transport shape only; Rust owns evidence policy
non_goals: No report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or summary-only wrapper
No provider/tool/verifier execution, workspace mutation, shell, git, network, or service expansion
No raw Product Charter, manifest, spec, ledger, prompt, provider, file, command, output, environment, absolute path, canonical path, or secret exposure
No milestone closeout in this implementation PR
rejected_alternatives: Adding a product evidence inspection RPC was rejected because the runtime decision path needs evidence authority, not observability.
Keeping runtime hard-coded Brownie artifact paths was rejected because it makes the runtime own project-specific strategy instead of enforcing a generic policy boundary.
Keeping caller-supplied categories as source of truth was rejected because it leaves product completion outside Rust authority.
Parsing raw Product Charter text into RPC output was rejected because it would leak artifact content and create a summary surface.
Broad runtime modularization was deferred so this remains a bounded vertical slice.
technical_debt: The generic project completion policy schema is intentionally minimal JSON; richer internal Product Charter modeling remains future M52 work.
crates/brownie-runtime/src/lib.rs remains large and should be split only in a cohesive future refactor.
M50.1 journey admission atomicity remains separate non-blocking technical debt.
next_capability_rationale: If accepted, the next M52 phase should harden freshness or broaden runtime-owned evidence categories only if it changes product-decision authority rather than adding an inspection wrapper.
